learning_outcomes.text: Explain the overall function of a tractor and derive sub-functions, representing their implementation in technical components. Recognize, represent, and analyze the tractor as a subsystem in the overall "human-tractor-implement-soil-plant" system. Recognize the relationships in this system, analyze the interactions occurring therein, and evaluate the interplay and dependencies of the individual components (including technical and economic design optimization).
Represent and draw conclusions from the interactions between chassis and soil, and between tractor and implement.

Explain the requirements of STVO and STVZO, as well as the ISOBUS standard ISO 11738 for tractors, and describe implementation possibilities. Recognize and highlight technical potentials for economic, ecological, and ergonomic improvements. Present elaborated results in a written report and a presentation. Summarize the contents of essential regulations and describe testing methods. Understand the different boundary conditions for analyzing the overall "human-tractor-implement-soil-plant" system. Identify suitable components and procedures and develop and discuss appropriate applications with regard to technical, ergonomic, and societal challenges.

Apply knowledge and understanding to professional activities and develop or further develop problem solutions in the use and application of tractors. This includes the application and activation of acquired knowledge, a critical understanding of knowledge, and a methodical expansion of knowledge.

Derive and define research questions in the field of tractor technology and application. Explain and justify the operationalization of research, apply research methods, and present and explain research results.
Present the results elaborated in cooperation within the project group in a clearly structured written report and a presentation.

Develop a professional self-image oriented towards the goals and standards of professional action in professional fields predominantly outside of science. Justify their own professional actions with theoretical and methodical knowledge and assess their own abilities, autonomously reflect situation-appropriate design and decision-making freedoms and use them under guidance. Recognize situational framework conditions of professional action and justify their decisions ethically responsible. Critically reflect on their professional actions regarding societal expectations and consequences.

syllabus_topics: Types of tractors: universal and special tractors, system vehicles
Functions of agricultural tractors: Pulling, Carrying, Guiding, Driving, Regulating

Tractor components: Chassis, Engine, Transmission (standard manual transmissions, continuously variable and power-split transmissions), Wheels and tires or belts and tracks, Cabin, Implement interfaces (incl. norms and regulations (e.g., STVO and STVZO))
Terramechanical fundamentals: Contact area pressure, stress distribution, as well as slip and traction coefficient in traction transfer, soil compaction
Contact and power transfer between tire/chassis and soil
Mechanical, hydraulic, and electrical implement drives, including their control and regulation
Electrics and Electronics: ISO 11783 and SAE J 1939
